source_text:
Πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν μὴ ὁμολογῇ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐν σαρκὶ ἐληλυθέναι, ἀντιχριστός ἐστιν: καὶ ὃς ἂν μὴ ὁμολογῇ τὸ μαρτύριον τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἐκ τοῦ διαβόλου ἐστίν: καὶ ὃς ἂν μεθοδεύῃ τὰ λόγια τοῦ κυρίου πρὸς τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας καὶ λέγῃ μήτε ἀνάστασιν μήτε κρίσιν, οὗτος πρωτότοκος ἐστι τοῦ σατανᾶ.
διὸ ἀπολιπόντες τὴν ματαιότητα τῶν πολλῶν καὶ τὰς ψευδοδιδασκαλίας ἐπὶ τὸν ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἡμῖν παραδοθέντα λόγον ἐπιστρέψωμεν, νήφοντες πρὸς τὰς εὐχὰς καὶ προσκαρτεροῦντες νηστείαις, δεήσεσιν αἰτούμενοι τὸν παντεπόπτην θεὸν μὴ εἰσενεγκεῖν ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ κύριος: Τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον, ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.
thought_title: Whoever denies Christ's flesh, the cross, or resurrection is of the devil
orientation: Polycarp is warning the Philippians against false teachers, and now states the tests by which such people are known.
pass_a_gloss: For every [one] who would not confess Jesus Christ in flesh to have come, antichrist is; and [the one] who would not confess the testimony of the cross, from the devil is; and [the one] who would distort the sayings of the Lord toward [his] own desires and would say neither resurrection nor judgment, this [one] firstborn is of Satan. Therefore, having left behind the vanity of the many and the false teachings, to the from [the] beginning to us handed-down word let us turn, being sober toward the prayers and persisting in fastings, with supplications asking the all-seeing God not to lead us into temptation, just as the Lord said: The spirit indeed [is] willing, but the flesh [is] weak.

choices.why: Glossary term; kept as antichrist per the brief.
Glossary term; 'testimony' chosen per the brief's vote.
Glossary term; kept as false teachings per the brief.
Captures the sense of manipulating or twisting the Lord's sayings for selfish ends.
Literal rendering of the compound adjective; conveys God's comprehensive oversight.

bible_refs.note: Τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον, ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής

pass_b_english: Anyone who will not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is an antichrist. Anyone who will not confess the testimony of the cross belongs to the devil. And anyone who twists the Lord's sayings to suit his own desires and says there is neither resurrection nor judgment—that man is the firstborn of Satan.

So let us abandon the vanity of the many and their false teachings, and turn back to the word that was handed down to us from the beginning. Let us be sober in prayer, persist in fasting, and in our petitions ask the all-seeing God not to lead us into temptation, as the Lord said: "The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak" (Matthew 26:41).

last_rejected.why: 'Firstborn of Satan' is literal and correct. The Greek 'πρωτότοκος' means firstborn, and 'τοῦ σατανᾶ' is genitive 'of Satan.' Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: πρωτότοκος means firstborn; τοῦ σατανᾶ is genitive of Satan. Translation is accurate.

last_rejected.why: 'δεήσεσιν' is dative plural 'petitions, prayers, supplications.' 'αἰτούμενοι' is 'asking.' The English 'in our petitions ask' is slightly redundant but captures both terms. However, this merges the participles awkwardly with 'let us be sober... persist... and... ask.' Actually the Greek has three participles: νήφοντες, προσκαρτεροῦντες, αἰτούμενοι, all dependent on ἐπιστρέψωμεν. The English makes them parallel imperatives, which changes the syntax but not necessarily the meaning. The 'in our petitions ask' is slightly awkward but conveys the sense.
last_rejected.ruling: Participles rendered as parallel imperatives with ἐπιστρέψωμεν; meaning preserved, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak
last_rejected.source_quote: Τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον, ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής
last_rejected.why: Standard translation of this saying. 'πρόθυμον' means ready, eager, willing. 'ἀσθενής' means weak, infirm. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Standard rendering of πρόθυμον/ἀσθενής; accurate translation of the biblical quotation.

last_rejected.why: 'πρὸς' here means 'toward, for the purpose of, to suit.' 'ἰδίας' is 'his own.' 'ἐπιθυμίας' is 'desires, lusts, cravings.' 'To suit his own desires' is idiomatic and correct.
last_rejected.ruling: πρὸς τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας correctly rendered as 'to suit his own desires'; normal meaning range.

last_rejected.why: 'ἀπολιπόντες' is aorist participle, 'having left behind, abandoned, forsaken.' 'Abandon' captures this. The English uses present 'let us abandon' where Greek has participle, but this is normal in literary translation to make it imperative in force with the following ἐπιστρέψωμεν.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπολιπόντες as 'abandon' with ἐπιστρέψωμεν is standard; participle to imperative is normal translation practice.

last_rejected.why: The Greek has 'τὰς ψευδοδιδασκαλίας' with no possessive. The English adds 'their' to connect with 'the many.' This is a slight addition but natural in English. However, 'their' implies the false teachings belong to 'the many,' which may be accurate contextually but is not explicit in the Greek. This is a minor addition.
last_rejected.ruling: Added 'their' is natural English connection to τῶν πολλῶν; minor pronoun, not a major error.
